hint.text: A conspiracy is a secret plan involving several people working together, often to achieve something wrong or illegal.
hint.label: Conspiracy

atoms.text: After a brief period of stability, raids escalated again in AD 367, with several groups attacking Roman Britain at the same time. Roman historians later called this period the Great Conspiracy.
Although it is referred to as a conspiracy, the different groups probably did not work together. Instead, they likely attacked around the same period because the Roman Empire had become weaker.
The Picts attacked from the north at Hadrian’s Wall, the Scots from the west and the Saxon raiders pushed through south-eastern forts from the coast.

hint.text: Most of what we know about the Great Conspiracy comes from Ammianus Marcellinus, who wrote about it about 20 years later. Modern historians think he likely exaggerated how organised the attacks were.
hint.sound: Most of what we know about the Great Conspiracy comes from Ahmie-ahnus Marsellinus, who wrote about it about 20 years later. Modern historians think he likely exaggerated how organised the attacks were.
hint.label: Did you know?

atoms.b: When the tribes ((++attacked surrendered)) together, some Roman soldiers helped them by rebelling against the empire.
Many soldiers were underfed and ((++underpaid overpaid)), so their loyalty to Rome began to crumble.
They abandoned their posts across Roman Britain, most famously at Hadrian’s Wall. This allowed the ((++Picts Romans)) to break through and raid Roman Britain!
The confusion also gave some enslaved people a chance to escape captivity. They joined together, setting fire to farms and ((++villas pyramids)) as they fled from the Romans.

atoms.b: The Roman emperor sent a general to Britain to regain control after the ((++Great Good)) Conspiracy. Although the ((++Romans raiders)) managed to restore order, the province remained difficult to defend.

atoms.text: By this point, the ongoing raids from tribes and rebellions among Roman soldiers had made things very difficult. Rome could no longer keep control of Britain while still defending the rest of the empire.
atoms.sound: By this point, the ongoing raids from tribes, and rebellions among Roman soldiers had made things very difficult. Rome could no longer keep control of Britain while still defending the rest of the empire.

atoms.text: By AD 400, the Roman Empire had withdrawn their soldiers from Hadrian’s Wall for the final time. In AD 410, after nearly 400 years of Roman rule, the Romans left Britain for good and never returned.

atoms.a: Which two reasons made the Great Conspiracy so difficult for the Romans?
b: ++The tribes attacked at the same time.
The Romans did not have any weapons.

feedback.finish: The Great Conspiracy did not end Roman Britain straight away, but it marked the beginning of the end of Roman rule.
